content: This medication may pass into breast milk, but it is unlikely to cause harm to a nursing infant. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests: While using this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, skin examinations, and Pap smears. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your medical condition may lead to complications in an emergency situation. Important Information Usage: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is used to treat certain types of arthritis (rheumatoid arthritis, arthritis of the spine, psoriatic arthritis), specific bowel diseases (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis), and a severe skin condition (chronic plaque psoriasis). These conditions involve the immune system attacking healthy tissues. Infliximab works by inhibiting the activity of a natural substance in the body called tumor necrosis factor-alpha. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting infliximab and each time you receive a refill. This medication is administered via injection into a vein over at least two hours, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, and response to treatment. Infusion reactions may occur during the administration of this drug. Your doctor may prescribe additional medications before each treatment to help prevent these side effects. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of infusion reactions, such as pain or swelling at the injection site, shortness of breath, flushing, chills, fever, or headache. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained in its preparation and administration by your healthcare professional. Do not shake the medication. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Use this medication regularly to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects may include headache, stomach pain, or nausea. Risks and Side Effects: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this drug may cause serious, potentially fatal liver disease. Heart problems, such as heart attacks, may occur during the infusion and up to 24 hours afterward. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using infliximab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other infliximab products, or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Infliximab may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have infections that can easily spread, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare professional that you are using infliximab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. This drug may pass into breast milk, but it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant.
